heading.en: Why does every living thing need a name?

hook.en: The mango you call "maavu" in Mysuru is "aam" in Delhi and "mango" in London. How would scientists across the *world* know they are talking about the same plant?
hook.kn: ಮೈಸೂರಿನಲ್ಲಿ "ಮಾವು" ಎಂದು ಕರೆಯುವ ಹಣ್ಣನ್ನು ದೆಹಲಿಯಲ್ಲಿ "ಆಮ್" ಎನ್ನುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಪ್ರಪಂಚದ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನಿಗಳು ಒಂದೇ ಸಸ್ಯದ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಮಾತನಾಡುತ್ತಿದ್ದಾರೆ ಎಂದು ಹೇಗೆ ತಿಳಿಯುತ್ತಾರೆ?

body.en: *Biodiversity* is the number and types of organisms present on earth. Between 1.7 and 1.8 million species have been described so far, and many more are still being discovered in forests, oceans and soil.
body.kn: ಭೂಮಿಯ ಮೇಲಿರುವ ಜೀವಿಗಳ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ ಮತ್ತು ಬಗೆಗಳೇ ಜೀವವೈವಿಧ್ಯ. ಇಲ್ಲಿಯವರೆಗೆ ಸುಮಾರು 1.7 ರಿಂದ 1.8 ಮಿಲಿಯನ್ ಪ್ರಭೇದಗಳನ್ನು ವಿವರಿಸಲಾಗಿದೆ.

narration.en: The same organism has different names in different languages and even in different villages, which causes confusion. Scientists therefore give each organism one scientific name that is used everywhere in the world, following agreed rules (ICBN for plants, ICZN for animals).
narration.kn: ಒಂದೇ ಜೀವಿಗೆ ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ಭಾಷೆಗಳಲ್ಲಿ, ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ಹಳ್ಳಿಗಳಲ್ಲೂ ಬೇರೆ ಹೆಸರುಗಳಿದ್ದು ಗೊಂದಲ ಉಂಟಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನಿಗಳು ಒಪ್ಪಿತ ನಿಯಮಗಳ (ಸಸ್ಯಗಳಿಗೆ ICBN, ಪ್ರಾಣಿಗಳಿಗೆ ICZN) ಪ್ರಕಾರ ಪ್ರತಿ ಜೀವಿಗೆ ವಿಶ್ವದೆಲ್ಲೆಡೆ ಬಳಸುವ ಒಂದು ವೈಜ್ಞಾನಿಕ ಹೆಸರು ನೀಡುತ್ತಾರೆ.

title.en: On the board: Diversity in the living world

say.en: Biodiversity means the number and the types of organisms present on earth.
About 1.7 to 1.8 million species have been described so far, and more are found every year.
One mango has many local names: maavu in Kannada, aam in Hindi, mango in English.
Scientists solve the confusion with one scientific name used all over the world.
The ICBN gives rules for naming plants; the ICZN for animals.

narration.en: Some features are shared by every living thing and by nothing non-living. Others have exceptions. Sort them.

prompt.en: Sort each feature: is it a defining property of living things, or does it have exceptions?
prompt.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಲಕ್ಷಣವನ್ನು ವಿಂಗಡಿಸಿ: ಇದು ಜೀವಿಗಳ ವ್ಯಾಖ್ಯಾನಾತ್ಮಕ ಲಕ್ಷಣವೇ, ಅಥವಾ ಇದಕ್ಕೆ ಅಪವಾದಗಳಿವೆಯೇ?

text.en: Metabolism: thousands of chemical reactions in the body
Consciousness: sensing and responding to the surroundings
Growth: increase in mass and number of cells
Increase in size (a sand mound or a crystal also grows)

explanation.en: Growth and reproduction are not defining: non-living crystals and mountains grow by accumulation, and mules, worker bees and infertile couples do not reproduce. Metabolism, cellular organisation and consciousness are found in every living thing and in no non-living thing.

ICZN: International Code of Zoological Nomenclature.

problem.en: A student sees a plant called "tulasi" in Karnataka and "holy basil" in an English book. Explain why a biologist would rather use its scientific name.

steps.en: Local names differ by region and language, so two people may not know they mean the same plant.
A scientific name is unique: one organism has only one valid name, used worldwide.
It is framed under ICBN rules, so any botanist anywhere can identify the plant correctly.

answer.en: Because the scientific name is unique and universal, while local names cause confusion.
